items.question: How do Wi-Fi QR codes connect devices automatically?
items.answer: The QR code encodes a standard ZXing Wi-Fi configuration payload (WIFI:T:...;S:...;P:...;;). When scanned with iOS Camera or Android, the device automatically parses the SSID and credentials to connect.

items.question: Is my network password saved or sent over the internet?
items.answer: Never. The QR code is generated 100% locally in your web browser. Note, however, that anyone who physically scans the code can view your network password in plain text.

items.question: How are special characters in SSIDs and passwords handled?
items.answer: In accordance with the ZXing Wi-Fi QR specification, characters including colons, semicolons, commas, and backslashes are escaped with a preceding backslash.

items.question: Can I print a guest Wi-Fi card to display?
items.answer: Yes. Use the "Print Guest Card" button to trigger a clean printable layout formatted specifically for tabletop or wall display.

items.question: Does this work for hidden Wi-Fi networks?
items.answer: Yes. Enabling the "Hidden Network" checkbox appends H:true to the configuration payload so devices scan for non-broadcasting SSIDs.

items.question: Are modern WPA3 networks supported?
items.answer: Yes. Modern mobile operating systems recognize the standard T:WPA token for all WPA, WPA2, and WPA3 Personal networks.

items.question: Can I generate a QR code for open networks without a password?
items.answer: Yes. Selecting the "None / Open" security option omits the password field and sets T:nopass, allowing guests to join open Wi-Fi with one tap.

items.question: What is the advantage of downloading SVG over PNG?
items.answer: SVG is an infinitely scalable vector format that ensures sharp, pixel-perfect printing on posters and signage at any physical print size.
